subject: lambda: Loading parameters. & rho: Correlation parameters (associated with covariance parameters).

messages.author: 5892b1018c4e4cfc
messages.subject: lambda: Loading parameters. & rho: Correlation parameters (associated with covariance parameters).
parts:
Hello,

On the help page of dpriors {blavaan}/?dpriors, there is both lambda and rho.

I am a bit confused. Are the lambda estimates the same as the rho estimates (diagnal)?

Especially noted that, in the following, the last two lines give me the same results:

m<-'model=~'
independents<-c("x1","x2","x3")
variables <- paste(independents, collapse = '+')
dataa<-HolzingerSwineford1939[,7:9]
CFA <- cfa(paste(m,variables,sep=''),data=dataa,
           std.lv=TRUE,missing = "fiml")

inspect(CFA,what="std")$lambda
standardizedSolution(CFA)[1:3,]



Second question: what's the difference of the following three? Are lambda, rho and prior all referring to factor loading/item-domain-correlation? Are they the same?
fit1 <- bcfa(model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939,dp = dpriors(lambda = "dbeta(4,1)"));
fit2 <- bcfa(model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939,dp = dpriors(rho= "dbeta(4,1)")); and

HS.model <- ' model  =~ prior("dbeta(4,1)")*x1 + prior("dbeta(4,1)")*x2 + prior("dbeta(4,1)")*x3'
fit3 <- bcfa(model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)



Thanks.
Hao

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: lambda: Loading parameters. & rho: Correlation parameters (associated with covariance parameters).
parts:
Hao,

lambda are the factor loadings, whereas "rho" is only used when we decompose a covariance matrix. For example, sometimes we take the residual covariance matrix (often called Theta) and decompose it into

Theta = D Rho D,

where D is a diagonal matrix of residual standard deviations and Rho is a correlation matrix (contains correlations between residual terms). Then the prior distribution for entries of Rho comes from the "rho" part of dpriors(). Technical details can be found here:

https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v085.i04

For your 1-factor model, the rho priors are not used. So your fit1 and fit3 should be the same model (lambda priors specified in two different ways), while fit2 just uses the default prior for lambda (dnorm(0,1e-2)). But the fit3 specification is a little funny because you have a prior on all three loadings, but the first loading is typically fixed to 1 for identification.

Ed
